## ctxloom remote edit

Change a remote's name, URL or forge binding

### Synopsis

Change a registered remote in place, rather than removing and re-creating it.

Editing a remote is safe for content already pulled from it: every lockfile
entry records its own URL, so nothing installed is repointed. It is also
irrelevant to trust, which is keyed to a signing identity and verified over
the bytes themselves — a remote is an address and carries no authority.

Renaming the default remote carries the default with it; the report says so.

```
ctxloom remote edit <name> [flags]
```

### Options

```
      --forge string   Rebind to a forge: github, git, or a configured forges: label (empty resolves from the URL host)
      --name string    Rename the remote (the default remote pointer follows)
      --url string     Change the repository URL
```
